body:
Hello, finally revisiting this :)

I think it's an interesting idea, but in addition to:

> I'm unclear where to draw the line on what goes in navigation params, and what we decide is too specific to only a few cases and so we leave out. (initiatorOrigin is only used for hand-off to external software, and multipart/x-mixed replace... maybe it's best left out too?)

I think restructuring at least "hand-off to external software" to take "a non-fetch scheme navigation params OR a navigation params" makes it slightly awkward to pull members from. In that algorithm for example, it seems to me that you either have to:

1. Do some up-front awkward stuff at the beginning of any algorithms that accepts this "union" type to pull out the actual type that was passed in, so that usages of the argument know whether to reference `non-fetch-navigation-params-url` vs `navigation-params-url`; OR....
2. Or if that's not what you had in mind — and you'd just _always_ reference members of this argument via the `navigation-params-*` prefix — then I think you have to do this mental trick where you have to remember that the argument you're pulling things from might be of the "subset" type, so you must limit yourself to only touching things inside `navigation-params-*` that you know are present in both types (navigation params & non-fetch scheme navigation params).

In that case since this PR only introduces a single variant of navigation params, I feel its approach — of a) introducing this variant, and b) keeping abstraction one level higher than "Handle external software", so that said algorithm accepts various parameters that could've come from anywhere — is a little simpler. I'm a little on the fence, but would prefer to just proceed.
